# MRK — Quantitative Fundamental Attractiveness Report
**Decision Date: 2026-07-24 | PIT data through 2026-07-23**

---

## 1. Revenue, Earnings, Margin, Cash-Flow, and Balance-Sheet Trajectory

**Revenue** is resilient. Q1 2026 revenue of $16.29B grew +4.9% YoY (vs. Q1 2025: $15.53B) and sits between Q2 2025 ($15.81B) and Q3 2025 ($17.28B). There is no revenue deterioration.

**Earnings collapsed in Q1 2026.** EPS diluted swung from +$2.01 (Q1 2025) and +$2.32 (Q3 2025) to **−$1.72** (Q1 2026). Net income was −$4.24B. Operating income was −$3.53B versus +$5.90B (Q1 2025) and +$6.75B (Q3 2025). The deterioration is entirely below gross profit: Q1 2026 gross profit was $12.09B (−0.2% YoY), implying operating expenses surged by roughly $9.4B relative to the prior-year quarter. This is almost certainly a large non-cash charge or impairment rather than a margin compression story, since gross margin held at ~74%.

**Operating cash flow remains healthy.** Q1 2026 OCF was $3.92B — positive despite the accounting loss — and grew +56.7% YoY (vs. Q1 2025: $2.50B). The prior quarter (Q3 2025) generated $7.82B. Free cash flow data is unavailable; operating cash flow is the proxy and it is constructive.

**Balance sheet:** Total equity fell from $51.91B (Q3 2025) to $45.93B (Q1 2026), a decline of ~$6B consistent with the Q1 loss plus dividends. Total liabilities rose from $77.64B to $82.75B. Note: Q1/Q2 2025 balance sheet data contain apparent anomalies (total liabilities reported as negative), so trend analysis is limited to the last two observations.

**TTM is unavailable** due to a fiscal-quarter gap in the supplied history (Q1→Q3→Q2→Q1 with a missing Q4). No trailing-twelve-month sum will be constructed.

## 2. Earnings Quality and Balance-Sheet Resilience

Earnings quality is currently **opaque**. The disconnect between flat gross profit (+$12.09B) and deeply negative operating income (−$3.53B) signals a ~$15.6B swing in below-the-line operating costs vs. ~$6.7B in prior quarters. The most plausible quant explanation is a one-time write-down or restructuring charge. Crucially, operating cash flow ($3.92B) remained positive and grew YoY, suggesting the underlying cash-generative franchise is intact and the loss is accounting-driven rather than cash-destructive.

Balance-sheet resilience is **adequate but deteriorating**. Equity of $45.93B supports total assets of $128.69B (equity ratio ~35.7%). The $6B quarterly equity erosion is concerning if repeated but manageable as a one-time event. Without knowing debt-maturity details (not supplied), the balance sheet appears solvent but less cushioned than a year ago.

## 3. Valuation Versus Own History (Ratios)

Valuation is at **extreme highs** relative to the company's own 365-day history:

| Metric | Latest (7/23) | Window Range | Position |
|--------|---------------|--------------|----------|
| PE diluted | 36.1x | 11.1–36.1x | **Maximum** |
| P/B | 7.0x | 4.0–7.0x | **Maximum** |
| Net margin | 13.6% | 10–30% | **Low end** |
| ROE | 19.5% | 20–40% | **Below range** |
| Earnings yield | 2.8% | — | Well below 10Y yield of 4.71% |

The PE ratio tripled from ~12x (Jul 2025) to 36x (Jul 2026). This expansion is mechanically driven by the denominator collapse (earnings impairment) rather than by price alone. P/B expanded from 4.4x to 7.0x over the same period while ROE fell from 36.1% to 19.5% — the market is paying a record multiple for deteriorating return on equity. The earnings yield of 2.8% is 191bp below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.71%, meaning the equity is not compensating holders for risk versus risk-free alternatives.

If the Q1 charge is one-time and earnings normalize to the prior ~$2.00/quarter run-rate (~$8.00 annualized), the forward PE at $130.48 would be ~16.3x — reasonable for a large-cap pharma. But that normalization is an assumption, not a fact in the supplied

# Qualitative Assessment: Merck & Co. (MRK)
**Decision Date: 2026-07-24 | Analyst: Qualitative Franchise Review**

---

## 1. Business / Franchise Read

Merck & Co. is a large-cap global pharmaceutical company with a diversified franchise spanning oncology, vaccines, cardiometabolic/infectious disease, and animal health. The company generated approximately $60.1 billion in FY2023 revenue (up ~15.6% YoY from ~$52.0B in FY2022), with the human health segment accounting for well over three-quarters of total sales. FY2025 U.S. human health sales represent 53% of the company's total (Morningstar, 2026-07-19). TTM revenue stands at ~$65.8 billion (Yahoo Finance, 2026-07-21).

**Keytruda dominance and concentration risk** are the defining franchise features. Keytruda, Merck's PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor, generated estimated sales exceeding $25 billion in FY2023 and is described as one of the highest-revenue prescription medicines globally (ad-hoc-news.de, 2026-07-19). In Q1 2026, Keytruda/QLEX sales rose 12% to $8.0 billion (pandaforecast.com / TipRanks earnings call summary, 2026-07-17). The drug is currently generating the highest revenue among head-and-neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) therapies, and that market is projected to grow at a 10.5% CAGR through 2036 (GlobeNewswire/DelveInsight, 2026-07-13). However, Keytruda now accounts for "over half of its sales," creating significant concentration risk that has prompted aggressive M&A (pandaforecast.com, 2026-07-17).

**Vaccine franchise** includes HPV, pneumococcal, and pediatric products, each generating more than $1 billion in annual FY2023 sales (ad-hoc-news.de, 2026-07-19). Vaccine revenue provides relative stability through routine immunization schedules, though GARDASIL declined 22% in Q1 2026, notably in China (TipRanks, 2026-07-17).

**Animal health** contributes several billion dollars annually and diversifies the business beyond human therapeutics, benefiting from global protein consumption and pet care trends. This segment is less correlated with human drug pipeline cycles.

The franchise reads as durable but lopsided: a world-class immuno-oncology and vaccine portfolio, but one whose near-term earnings power is heavily concentrated in a single product approaching patent expiry.

---

## 2. Recent Dated Developments

**Q1 2026 earnings** (reported 2026-04-30, referenced across multiple sources): Revenue of $16.29–$17.5 billion (sources vary on adjusted vs. GAAP; $16.29B per Barchart/DailyPolitical, $17.5B per ad-hoc-news update citing IR). GAAP EPS was -$1.28, reflecting a ~$9 billion one-time Cidara charge and an expected ~$5.8 billion R&D impact from the proposed Terns Pharmaceuticals acquisition (TipRanks, 2026-07-17). Adjusted figures were stronger, with the company topping consensus estimates by $0.19. Revenue grew ~4.9% YoY.

**FY2026 guidance** was raised/narrowed to $5.04–$5.16 adjusted EPS (DailyPolitical, 2026-07-20). The guidance incorporates IPR&D charges from the Terns deal.

**Pipeline and regulatory milestones**: FDA-approved Idvynso; priority reviews for I-DXd; multiple WELIREG filings; and the Terns acquisition positioning Merck in the CML space with TERN-701 (pandaforecast.com, 2026-07-17). The LITESPARK-012 readout failed, representing a pipeline setback. Merck's industrial synthesis of enlicitide (a macrocyclic peptide for LDL lowering) was noted as a significant innovation achievement with multibundant-dollar commercial potential (pandaforecast.com, 2026-07-17).

**Market context**: MRK stock has returned ~66.5% over one year (Yahoo Finance, 2026-07-21) and ~23% YTD versus ~11% for the S&P 500, reflecting strong investor confidence. Market capitalization stands at ~$317–322 billion. Forward P/E is ~48.3x, which appears elevated for a company facing a major patent cliff in 2028.

**Next earnings date**: August 4, 2026 (Barchart, 2026-07-21).

---

## 3. Material Qualitative Risks and Offsets

**Key risks:**

- **Keytruda patent expiry (~2028)**: This is the central structural risk. With Keytruda representing over half of revenue, loss of exclusivity will invite biosimilar/generic competition and could compress revenue materially. The market's forward P/E of ~48x appears to price in significant continued growth despite this cliff.
- **Concentration risk**: Beyond Keytruda, GARDASIL's 22% decline signals vulnerability in the vaccine franchise, particularly in China. A failed late-stage trial (LITESPARK-012) further narrows pipeline optionality.
- **Pricing and reimbursement headwinds**: U.S. drug pricing policy scrutiny, payer negotiations, and potential legislative changes remain structural risks for all branded pharma, and Merck's high-revenue specialty products are particularly exposed.
- **M&A execution risk**: The Terns acquisition carries study outcomes risk, legal exposure, and bidding execution risk (Simply Wall St, 2026-07-17). The ~$5.8B R&D charge and $9B Cidara charge indicate heavy near-term costs that depress GAAP earnings.
- **Competition**: 180+ companies are developing PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors (GlobeNewswire/DelveInsight, 2026-07-21), and Bristol-Myers Squibb's Opdivo competes directly in immuno-oncology.

**Key offsets:**

- **Pipeline breadth**: Described as featuring "over 20 potential blockbusters" (pandaforecast.com, 2026-07-17), with assets spanning oncology, immunology, cardiometabolic disease, and vaccines. The enlicitide program and TERN-701 offer diversification vectors.
- **Oncology trio generating $8.23B in Q1** with 12.1% YoY growth, demonstrating the broader oncology franchise's momentum beyond Keytruda alone.
- **Diversified segments**: Animal health and vaccines provide cyclical resilience and recurring demand profiles.
- **Capital allocation flexibility**: Strong balance sheet, consistent dividend ($3.40 annual forward, ~2.6% yield), and strategic M&A capacity. The $70B revenue target by mid-2030s signals management confidence in pipeline-to-commercial conversion (pandaforecast.com, 2026-07-17).
- **Structural market tailwinds**: Autoimmune therapeutics market projected to reach $137.85B by 2035 (GlobeNewswire, 2026-07-15); oral obesity therapies market to $6.32B by 2030 (GlobeNewswire, 2026-07-15); HNSCC market growing at 10.5% CAGR — all addressable by Merck's pipeline.

---

## 4. Qualitative Assessment

**Assessment: Neutral-to-Slightly-Positive on fundamental attractiveness, with significant caution on valuation.**

Merck possesses a genuinely world-class franchise: Keytruda is arguably the most commercially successful immuno-oncology therapy in history, the vaccine business provides defensive recurring revenue, and the animal health segment adds diversification. The company's R&D pipeline is broad, its balance sheet is strong, and management is actively pursuing acquisitions (Terns, previously Verona Pharma at ~$10B) to address the patent cliff.

However, the narrative reveals a franchise in a precarious transition. Keytruda's dominance, while a testament to past execution, creates an outsized concentration risk heading into a 2028 patent cliff. The pipeline, while described as large, carries meaningful execution uncertainty — one late-stage failure (LITESPARK-012) has already occurred, and the Terns deal introduces ~$5.8B in R&D charges with uncertain outcomes. GARDASIL's weakness in China adds another near-term headwind. At a forward P/E of ~48x with TTM EPS of ~$5.47 and FY2026 guidance of $5.04–$5.16, the market appears to be pricing in aggressive pipeline conversion that has not yet been proven.

The franchise quality is high; the competitive position in oncology is leading. But the structural risk-reward at current valuation (post-66% one-year rally) appears less compelling, as much of the positive pipeline optionality may already be embedded in expectations. The upcoming August 4 earnings will be an important near-term data point.

---
